title: Brand Report Card Exercise
author_source: Elizabeth Bornheimer & Kevin Lane Keller; Harvard Business School; Product #501004; 15 Aug 2000; 11 pp.; exercise
note: Classic companion exercise to Keller's HBR article 'The Brand Report Card': students rate a brand on Keller's ten brand-equity attributes, isolate its distinctive traits and decide which areas matter most for improving performance. Short (11 pp.) and structured like a mini brand audit, so it works as a template for student audit projects.
course_use: Kick-off session of a brand audit project: each team grades its own audit brand with the report card, then compares. Paid: USD 8.95 per copy (less via HBP Educator account, up to 50% academic discount); check WU licence/coursepack

title: Dove: Evolution of a Brand
author_source: John A. Deighton; Harvard Business School Case 508-047; Oct 2007 (rev. Mar 2008); 13 pp.; case
note: Follows Dove's move from a functional soap to a masterbrand with a point of view (Real Beauty) and its stretch into new categories. Covers the research that led to the repositioning (psychologists plus a 3,000-woman study in 10 countries) and how Unilever handled online controversy. Won an ECCH/Case Centre Marketing award in 2012.
course_use: Case discussion on brand meaning, the brand exploratory, and masterbrand extension limits; pair it with current Dove tracking or press coverage for a then-vs-now audit. Paid via HBP (~USD 9-12); check WU licence

title: Barbie: Reviving a Cultural Icon at Mattel
author_source: Elie Ofek, Ryann Noe, Sarah Mehta; Harvard Business School Case 525-006; 6 Aug 2024 (rev. Jan 2025); 30 pp.; abridged version 525-020 also available
note: Recent brand revitalization case. It contrasts decades of criticism (narrow beauty standards, gender stereotypes) and mixed results from earlier diversification with the 2023 film-driven revival. The decision: how to sustain the momentum, and whether the approach can be transferred to other brands in Mattel's portfolio. Rich material for brand associations and brand-portfolio thinking.
course_use: Main case discussion on brand revitalization and on auditing the associations a brand carries; the abridged version suits undergraduates. Paid: USD 11.95 per copy; check WU licence

title: Burberry's Digital Strategy
author_source: Don Sull, Stefano Turconi, Sanam Zanjani; London Business School (via HBP) #LBS330; 1 Mar 2022; 36 pp.; case
note: Covers the 2006-2014 Burberry turnaround under Ahrendts and Bailey: winning back a brand diluted by licensing and by the 'chav' check, refocusing on heritage and the trench coat, targeting millennials and building digital capabilities. It ends in 2015 with mixed results and Bailey as combined CEO/CCO. A standard case on regaining brand control after an audit shows dilution.
course_use: Case discussion: reconstruct the 2006 brand audit the case implies (inventory: licences, products; exploratory: associations), then judge the fixes. Paid: USD 11.95; check WU licence

title: LEGO (A): The Crisis
author_source: Stefan Thomke, Jan W. Rivkin, Daniela Beyersdorfer; Harvard Business School case (A), 2013 (B/C follow-ups exist); case
note: LEGO near bankruptcy (2003-04 sales -26%, heavy losses); new CEO Knudstorp must diagnose why diversification diluted the brick and craft a back-to-core strategy. Shows how a brand/portfolio audit feeds a turnaround. One failed and one successful turnaround attempt give a natural before/after comparison.
course_use: Case discussion on brand-core identification and portfolio rationalisation; combine with the free AEF LEGO 'Rebuild the World' case for brand tracking. Paid via HBP (~USD 9-12); check WU licence

title: Rebuild the World: How LEGO Reinvented Creativity in Play (Parts A & B)
author_source: Jia Li (Wake Forest University) & Michael Moynihan (LEGO Group / HBS), with Marcia Soling; ANA Educational Foundation (AEF) case history; covers 2016-2019; case + teaching note
note: Free case with real exhibits for brand measurement: Part A covers the 2016-17 sales stall and repositioning toward creativity for low-affinity parents; Part B covers measuring the global 'Rebuild the World' campaign and reporting to the board. Appendices: tracking-study response data, media effectiveness data and purchase data (simulated), plus a teaching note/discussion guide PDF.
course_use: Hands-on brand tracking exercise: students analyse the tracking appendix and build a board-level brand health report. Free download, no login

title: Old Spice: Revitalizing Glacial Falls
author_source: Derek D. Rucker & David DuBois; Kellogg School of Management case 5-411-752 (KEL619); 11 Nov 2011; case
note: Compact repositioning decision. Glacial Falls, the worst-performing scent in 2008, risks delisting. Should P&G keep current users or target new ones, and should it change the scent (sensory) or the positioning (cognitive)? Outcome: relaunched as 'Swagger', with strong sales according to WARC/Effie. A good test of positioning statements and multi-level branding.
course_use: Case discussion (60-75 min) on revitalization options; follow with the 2014 sequel case. Paid via HBP/Kellogg (~USD 9-12); check WU licence

title: Old Spice: Repeating Success in the Face of Competitive Threat
author_source: Derek D. Rucker & Mauricio O'Connell; Kellogg School of Management #KEL786; 16 May 2014; 10 pp.; case
note: Sequel (2009-10): after Swagger, should the team push Swagger, another scent, the umbrella brand or body wash, and should it react to Unilever's Dove Men+Care Super Bowl ad? Students play the assistant brand manager. Good for brand architecture (umbrella vs. sub-brand) and competitive brand audits.
course_use: Second session after the Glacial Falls case, or a stand-alone brand architecture discussion. Paid: USD 11.95; check WU licence

title: Managing Brand Crisis: Bud Light Cracks Open a Can of Controversy
author_source: Kimberly Whitler, Dan Baum, Emily Pasquinelli; Darden Business Publishing case M-1043; 29 Nov 2023; 18 pp.; case
note: First business-school case on the 2023 Dylan Mulvaney 'Easy Carry Contest' backlash, laid out as a timeline with decision points. Covers influencer-brand fit, core-user alienation and reputation recovery, with effects on AB InBev's market cap. Pairs well with public YouGov BrandIndex data (Impression -20 points) for a data-driven audit.
course_use: Case discussion on target-user fit and brand crisis; students add YouGov/Brand Finance numbers and write a post-crisis brand audit. Paid via Darden store (price shown at checkout); check WU licence

title: Bud Light academic case study package (MASB)
author_source: Marketing Accountability Standards Board (MASB); white paper + PPT with discussion questions/teaching guide + intro video; 2023/24
note: Practitioner-built teaching package that links damaged brand preference to a lasting drop in sales volume, using MASB's brand investment & valuation logic. It shows how brand-preference tracking predicts financial outcomes, which is the 'why audit' argument in numbers.
course_use: Complements the Darden case; use the white paper as pre-reading on brand metrics → financial outcomes. White paper downloadable free; full academic package on request (info@themasb.org)

title: Red Bull
author_source: Richard Johnson, Paul W. Farris, Jordan Mitchell; Darden School of Business #UV2928; 13 Jan 2003; 12 pp.; abridged version UV6672 (2013, ~8 pp.)
note: Classic case on non-traditional brand building (word of mouth, events) that created the functional energy drink category, ending with how to answer US competition. A strong Austrian brand example for WU students and good for discussing sources of brand equity.
course_use: Case discussion on brand building/brand equity sources for an Austrian brand; use as the 'origin' before the LBS 2022 case. Paid: USD 11.95; check WU licence

title: Red Bull Spreads its Wiiings
author_source: Nader Tavassoli; London Business School case CS-22-016; Sep 2022; 10 pp.; winner Case Centre Marketing Award 2025
note: Brand-extension and brand-architecture case: Red Bull 35 years on, with energy-drink variants, the Organics range and the AlphaTauri fashion brand, including an F1 team renaming. Students judge brand-extension fit and how sub-brands feed back into parent brand equity. Teaching PPT with 7 videos available to educators.
course_use: Session on brand architecture/extension audits; good for WU because of the Austrian brand. Paid via LBS/Case Centre/HBP (price after login); teaching slides via cases@london.edu

title: Red Bull: The Anti-Brand Brand
author_source: Sophie Coughlan, Nirmalya Kumar, Nader Tavassoli; London Business School; ranked #14 in The Case Centre's all-time Top 50
note: Best-selling case on how Red Bull built an iconic brand while avoiding traditional advertising. A strong base for mapping Red Bull's brand elements and associations in a brand inventory exercise.
course_use: Alternative to the Darden case for the brand-inventory part of an audit; available via LBS Publishing/The Case Centre (paid, ~GBP/USD 10-15); check WU licence

title: The logo change at Gap North America
author_source: Irene Pollach (Aarhus University); The CASE Journal / Emerald, 2016 (DOI 10.1108/TCJ-11-2014-0065); teaching note in Emerald Teaching Notes vol. 12(2), pp. 214-220
note: Teaching case on the October 2010 Gap logo change, reversed within about a week after a social-media backlash. Covers brand life cycle and the effect of a logo change on brand equity, associations and positioning. A teaching note exists. For graduate or advanced undergraduate students who already know branding.
course_use: Short case discussion on brand elements in the brand inventory and on the risk of changing distinctive assets. Emerald case collection, so check WU licence

title: Tropicana's Product (Re)Design: The Packaging Mistake
author_source: IBS Case Development Centre (IBSCDC) case OM0022; Dec 2009; teaching note & assignment available
note: Covers the January 2009 Tropicana Pure Premium carton redesign (orange-with-straw dropped) and its reversal within two months. IRI data cited in the press show unit sales -20% and about USD 33 m lost. The best-known example of an unaudited change to distinctive assets.
course_use: Short case paired with the Ehrenberg-Bass distinctive-asset grid; students run a mini fame/uniqueness test on their audit brand's assets. Paid (low-cost IBSCDC case); short ICMR caselet CLMM047 as alternative

title: Himalaya Drug Company: Repositioning an Herbal Soap
author_source: S. Ramesh Kumar, Venkata Seshagiri Rao, Narayana Trinadh Kotturu (IIM); Ivey Publishing #W13661; 11 Apr 2014; 8 pp.
note: One of the few cases built on consumer perception survey data versus two main competitors. Students read the brand image data and recommend a repositioning to rebuild brand equity, which is in effect the analysis step of a brand audit.
course_use: Data-interpretation exercise in the brand exploratory phase (perceptual comparison); 45-60 min. Paid: USD 11.95; check WU licence

title: Rasurel: Reviving an Ageing Brand
author_source: Amitava Chattopadhyay & Séverine de Wulf; INSEAD case ref. 5252; Dec 2004; 19 pp.
note: European (French) ageing swimwear brand inside lingerie firm Lejaby. The new marketing director must decide whether and how to reposition it and launch the Summer 2004 collection. Works for introductory positioning and for advanced repositioning plus organisational alignment behind the brand promise.
course_use: Classic European revitalization case for MBA/master classes; good for practising the 'reposition vs. retire' decision after an audit. Paid via INSEAD/Case Centre; check WU licence

title: Gucci's Turnaround: Repositioning and Rebuilding the Company
author_source: June Cotte & Jessica Zhang; Ivey Publishing #W18546; 12 Sep 2018; 10 pp.
note: Gucci in 2014: operating profit down three quarters in a row, and the CEO and creative director gone. The new CEO (Jan 2015) must decide whether to reposition and whether to hire the creative director from inside or outside. A clean luxury-brand repositioning decision.
course_use: Case discussion on luxury brand revitalization; can be paired with the 2021 SMU Gucci case for the outcome. Paid: USD 11.95; check WU licence

title: Gucci: Staying Relevant in Luxury over a Century
author_source: Nirmalya Kumar & Sheetal Mittal; Singapore Management University (distributed via HBP); 2021
note: Follow-up view: after the 2015 Bizzarri/Michele overhaul, Gucci tripled sales and quadrupled profits by end-2019. The question is how to keep a heritage luxury brand relevant. Useful for long-term brand tracking and the risks of trend-driven revitalization.
course_use: Second session or written assignment comparing pre-/post-2015 brand positioning. Paid via SMU/HBP; check WU licence

title: Volkswagen Emission Scandal: Reputation Recovery and Recall Strategy
author_source: Rachna Shah, Gaganpreet Singh, Sandeep Puri; Ivey Publishing case 9B17M052; 2017
note: German brand-reputation crisis: after the EPA notice on EA 189 diesel engines (Sept 2015), new CEO Matthias Müller must recover VW's reputation and plan the recall. A brand-trust audit after a crisis. Pair it with Gallup's 2015 'Can VW salvage a damaged brand' analysis.
course_use: Case discussion on brand trust and reputation audits after a crisis. Paid via Ivey/HBP (~USD 9-12); check WU licence. Alternative: INSEAD 'Volkswagen: Diesel Emissions - A Whiff of Scandal' (Jarisch & Kaiser 2017, governance focus)

title: Volkswagen: Diesel Emissions - A Whiff of Scandal
author_source: D. Jarisch & K. Kaiser; INSEAD case; 26 Jun 2017; with PowerPoint slides & embedded videos
note: Shows VW as a much-loved brand with green credentials, then the cheat on about 11 m cars, costs above EUR 16 bn and resignations. The focus is governance and culture rather than brand measurement, but it gives the setting for a 'trust regained?' brand audit.
course_use: Background case for a session on corporate brand reputation; teaching slides available. Paid via INSEAD/Case Centre; check WU licence

title: Restructuring Unilever: The 'Path To Growth' Strategy
author_source: ICMR (IBS Center for Management Research) case BSTR095; 2004; 17 pp.; period 2000-2003; no teaching note
note: Brand portfolio rationalisation, the textbook example: Unilever's 1999/2000 plan to cut from about 1,600 to about 400 core brands within the EUR 5 bn 'Path to Growth' programme. Use with current news on Unilever's focus on 30 'power brands' (70%+ of sales) and its ice-cream spin-off for a then/now portfolio audit.
course_use: Portfolio-audit session: students classify a brand portfolio (keep/invest/divest). Paid: INR 500 (~USD 11)

title: Peloton Interactive, Inc.: Creating the Immersive Connected-Fitness Category
author_source: Robert J. Dolan; Harvard Business School case (c. 2020, ~20 pp.); discussed in HBS Working Knowledge
note: Category creation and premium brand building, then the post-pandemic slump (losses, USD 750 m borrowing). Dolan's verdict: Peloton should have kept things simple. Useful for auditing a brand whose equity rests on a community and a lifestyle promise.
course_use: Case discussion or group assignment: post-2022 Peloton brand health check. Paid via HBP (~USD 9-12); check WU licence

title: World of Swarovski
author_source: Case study deposited in HAL/HALSHS (French open archive), bilingual EN/FR; marketing-plan case
note: Free Austrian-brand case: Swarovski (founded 1895) trying to establish itself in the global jewellery market against strong competition. Students build segmentation, targeting and positioning. Update it with the Dec 2024 IMD interview with CEO Alexis Nasard on the 'modern pop-luxury' repositioning (tiered collections, 2023 revenue EUR 1.83 bn).
course_use: Free group assignment on an Austrian brand: audit Swarovski before and after its 2020s repositioning. Free (open archive)

title: How the Dylan Mulvaney controversy hit Bud Light's brand (YouGov BrandIndex)
author_source: YouGov BrandIndex US analysis, 31 Aug 2023; public article
note: Public brand-health tracking data from 1 Apr-11 Jun 2023. Index 7.7 → -8.4; Impression 6.2 → -14 (-20.2); Consideration 14.1 → 10.9. Competitor Stella Artois only -3.5 on Impression. Age split: over 50s -21.5 vs. 18-34 -10.8. Also benchmarks Brewdog UK. A ready-made exhibit for crisis brand audits.
course_use: Data exhibit with the Darden Bud Light case: students read the tracking charts and judge damage by segment. Free

title: As NFL football returns, Bud Light sees a much-needed rebound (YouGov)
author_source: YouGov US article 47335, Sept 2023
note: Follow-up tracking. Bud Light regains some ground and tops Ad Awareness before NFL Kickoff 2023, and 8.9% of NFL fans say they bought it. Pair with sales data (-28% in the four weeks to 9 Dec 2023, per press) to show that perception and behaviour can diverge.
course_use: Discussion: does a recovery in awareness mean recovered brand equity? Free

title: Jaguar's brand reset has got the UK talking and consideration has ticked up (YouGov)
author_source: YouGov UK BrandIndex article 51062, 5 Dec 2024 (data 11 Nov-1 Dec 2024)
note: Post-rebrand tracking for the 19 Nov 2024 'Copy Nothing' launch. Attention 7.8 → 21.9 (18-34: 7.2 → 27.8); WOM exposure roughly doubled; Buzz fell among all UK adults but rose among 18-34 (2.7 → 9.2); Consideration 4.3 → 6.1. Shows that awareness spikes and sentiment can move in opposite directions.
course_use: Rebranding post-mortem exercise: students judge whether the Jaguar rebrand 'worked' using funnel metrics. Free

title: How an iconic brand pivots toward a new reality (Swayable Jaguar test)
author_source: Swayable Insights; randomized experiment with 7,186 US consumers, 2024/25
note: Randomized test of old vs. new Jaguar branding. Gen Z/Millennials showed higher consideration toward the new identity than Gen X, and favourability was not significantly disrupted. Teaches the difference between social-media outrage and measured brand effects.
course_use: Methods discussion: social listening vs. experimental testing in brand audits. Free

title: The decline of X: Musk's rebrand wipes billions in brand value (Brand Finance)
author_source: Brand Finance press release (Media 50 2024), 12 Sep 2024
note: Twitter → X post-mortem in valuation terms. Brand value USD 5.7 bn (Jan 2022) → 3.9 bn (2023) → 673 m (2024); Brand Strength Index -12.7 points to 56.9/100, with weaker familiarity, reputation and recommendation. Ad revenue down from more than USD 1 bn to about USD 600 m per quarter.
course_use: Example for linking brand strength metrics to financial value; critique the method in class. Free

title: Tropicana packaging fiasco: IRI sales data (Ad Age via Bloomberg)
author_source: Ad Age reporting reprinted by Bloomberg, 2 Apr 2009 (IRI data 1 Jan-22 Feb 2009)
note: Hard numbers for the Tropicana rebrand failure. Pure Premium unit sales -20%, dollar sales -19% (about USD 33 m) in under two months, with Minute Maid, Florida's Natural and Tree Ripe gaining. The redesign was scrapped on 23 Feb 2009. Ehrenberg-Bass cites about USD 26.3 m in lost sales.
course_use: Lecture example on distinctive assets in the brand inventory; pair with the Gap logo case. Free to read (Bloomberg may be metered)

title: Brands of Distinction: the Distinctive Asset Grid (Ehrenberg-Bass)
author_source: Jenni Romaniuk, Ehrenberg-Bass Institute for Marketing Science; article (republished from unisabusiness)
note: Introduces the Distinctive Asset Grid (fame × uniqueness: use or lose / invest / avoid / test or ignore). Examples include McDonald's arches, Nike swoosh, Disney castle, Coca-Cola script, Cadbury purple and Tropicana's lost packaging. This is the measurement logic for auditing brand elements.
course_use: Method input for the brand inventory: teams run a small unprompted asset-recognition survey for their audit brand. Free

title: Mastercard drops its name from the logo (symbol brand, 2019)
author_source: Dezeen, 10 Jan 2019; Pentagram identity (2016 redesign, 2019 symbol-only)
note: A positive distinctive-asset case. The decision rested on research showing more than 80% of people recognise the interlocking circles without the name, so the symbol-only mark was used on cards, at acceptance points and on sponsorships. A clean example of asset 'fame' data driving an identity decision.
course_use: Contrast with Tropicana/Gap: when is it safe to drop or change brand elements? Free

title: Brand Finance Austria 25 2026: Austria's top brands reach historic high, led by Red Bull
author_source: Brand Finance press release, Vienna, 8 Sep 2026; ISO 10668 royalty-relief method, ISO 20671 brand strength
note: Current Austrian brand-value ranking. Top 25 worth EUR 46.8 bn (+16%). Red Bull EUR 10.6 bn (+22%), Erste 7.9 bn, Raiffeisen 3.9 bn, A1 2.5 bn, ÖBB 2.1 bn; BAWAG PSK fastest-growing (+39%). The release spells out the 7-step valuation method with BSI → royalty rate.
course_use: Local data source for WU audit projects (brand value as one outcome metric); discussion of methods. Free press release; full report paid

title: Österreichische Markenwert-Studie 2026 (European Brand Institute)
author_source: European Brand Institute (EBI), 23rd edition, presented 1 Jul 2026; coverage news.at
note: Second Austrian valuation with very different numbers: Red Bull about EUR 20.1 bn (vs. 10.6 bn at Brand Finance), Novomatic 3.94 bn, Erste +26.6%. Top 10 also includes Spar, ÖBB, Swarovski, Raiffeisen, Verbund, XXXLutz, OMV. 180 companies from 16 sectors; ÖBB 'most sustainable brand' for the 7th time.
course_use: Compare EBI vs. Brand Finance for the same brands: why do valuation methods diverge? Free (press coverage)

title: Anholt-Ipsos Nation Brands Index 2022: Österreich auf Platz 16
author_source: Ipsos Austria press release, 7 Dec 2022 (NBI, 15th year, 60 countries)
note: Nation-brand audit for Austria across six dimensions (exports, governance, culture, people, tourism, immigration/investment). Austria ranks 16th, driven by tourism, culture and heritage and effective administration, while its people are not seen as especially friendly. Includes the Russia 27 → 58 drop as an example of a crisis effect. Note: the most recent Austria-specific release found is 2022.
course_use: Place/nation brand audit exercise; compare with WienTourismus positioning. Free

title: Vienna as a brand: WienTourismus brand positioning ('Now. Forever.' / 'Encouraging Enjoyment')
author_source: WienTourismus (Vienna Tourist Board) B2B site; brand relaunch 2016 with brand booklet/brand manual
note: City-brand case in Vienna. The brand was repositioned toward customer benefit and emotion ('the experiences of a city without the stress factors of a city'), with the brand core 'Encouraging Enjoyment', claim 'JETZT. FÜR IMMER', and new logo/CD. The 2016 brand booklet PDF is downloadable from b2b.wien.info. Related: the 2025 'Optimum Tourism' visitor-economy strategy.
course_use: Group assignment: city brand audit of Vienna (inventory from brand manual + exploratory via NBI/tourist surveys). Free

title: Stadt Wien: Markenstrategie & Markenarchitektur (CD-Manual)
author_source: Stadt Wien, Corporate Design Manual, section Markenstrategie/Markenarchitektur
note: A public umbrella-brand system (Dachmarke): the city brand is the most visible and departmental brands are absorbed into it (coat of arms + 'Stadt Wien' wordmark + descriptor). A real brand-architecture document that can be audited, and it sits alongside the separate WienTourismus brand.
course_use: Brand architecture exercise: map the Vienna brand family (city vs. tourism vs. Wiener Linien etc.). Free

title: Lidl: When the challenger becomes a British staple (IPA Effectiveness Awards 2024)
author_source: IPA Effectiveness Awards 2024 paper, published on WARC, 7 Oct 2024
note: Repositioning documented with brand tracking: Lidl GB moves from 'surprising discounter' to 'quality democratiser'. Market share +2.1 pp, consideration +5 pp, shopper penetration +4.4 pp, incremental revenue +68%. Shows how effectiveness papers link tracking to business results.
course_use: Model for the 'recommendations & measurement' section of a student audit. Free summary on WARC; full paper via WARC/IPA (check WU access)

title: IPA Effectiveness Awards 2024 winners (Grand Prix: McCain, adam&eveDDB)
author_source: IPA news release, Oct 2024; papers via IPA/WARC
note: Grand Prix McCain: long-term emotional brand building reduced price elasticity by 47%, raised base sales by 44% and delivered GBP 26 m net profit over nine years. The problem the brand had to fix: shoppers searched for 'oven chips' rather than 'McCain', i.e. weak brand salience. The award database (79 entries) is a source of real tracking-based cases.
course_use: Source pool: each audit team picks an IPA paper from its category as a benchmark. Free list; papers via WARC/IPA (check WU access)

title: Kantar BrandZ Most Valuable Global Brands 2026
author_source: Kantar BrandZ, 2026 report (Global Top 100)
note: Survey-based brand valuation (Meaningful-Different-Salient framework). Top 100 worth USD 13.1 tn (+22%); Google returns to No. 1; Zara overtakes Nike in apparel; Hermès overtakes Louis Vuitton in luxury; Louis Vuitton and Chanel are the only European losers. A good contrast to Brand Finance and Interbrand methods.
course_use: Benchmark source for audit projects; discuss consumer-equity vs. financial valuation. Free summary; full report free with registration

title: Telekom Austria stellt die gesamte Gruppe auf die Marke A1 um (EUR 350 m write-off)
author_source: Leadersnet.at, 20 Sep 2017; A1 Telekom Austria Group announcement
note: Austrian brand-architecture decision with hard numbers: more than 10 local brands migrated to a single A1 brand after 'extensive market and brand analyses', with EUR 350 m of local brand value written off. Follow-ups: 2023 design refresh with Saffron; A1 now 4th in Brand Finance Austria 2026 (EUR 2.5 bn).
course_use: Case vignette on brand portfolio consolidation (house of brands → branded house). Free

title: Merkur wird BILLA PLUS: REWE Austria rebranding 2021
author_source: REWE Group Austria press release, 28 Jan 2021; master thesis FH Wien der WKW 'Opportunities and risks of rebranding in food retailing - MERKUR to BILLA PLUS' (ECR Award 2023, 2nd place)
note: Austrian retail brand-architecture move: the 52-year-old Merkur brand is retired into BILLA PLUS (April 2021) to remove duplicate structures, saving a double-digit EUR million amount. An FH Wien thesis measured consumer evaluation via a representative online survey. In Brand Finance Austria 2025, Billa was the fastest-growing brand (+70% to EUR 2 bn).
course_use: Local vignette for discussing brand retirement/migration; students can audit BILLA vs. BILLA PLUS perception today. Free

title: Sample brand audit: Rolex (Keller, Strategic Brand Management)
author_source: Kevin Lane Keller, Strategic Brand Management, 4th ed. (Pearson 2013), pp. ~315-321; referenced as model in Macquarie University unit guide
note: The standard textbook model of a complete brand audit (brand inventory: portfolio, elements, product, price, IMC, distribution; brand exploratory: consumer knowledge, brand resonance pyramid, competitive analysis, recommendations). The Macquarie unit guide shows how a course turns it into an assignment template.
course_use: Template for the student brand audit report structure; textbook via WU library. Unit guide free online

title: Brand audit: A case study of Lacasa in Spain
author_source: Journal of Brand Strategy (Henry Stewart Publications / HSTalks), applied brand audit article
note: A published, complete Keller-style brand audit of a mid-sized European FMCG brand (Spanish chocolate maker Lacasa) ending in three concrete recommendations. It is close to what students produce and works as a worked example at the right scale.
course_use: Model answer/pre-reading before students write their own audit. Subscription (HSTalks/Journal of Brand Strategy), so check WU licence

title: Bud Light boycott: social listening data (The Social Element via Fox Business)
author_source: Fox Business, April 2023, citing The Social Element
note: Social-listening numbers for a brand audit. Bud Light had 1.08 m social mentions in the 11 days after the Mulvaney video vs. 20,400 in the 11 days before (mostly Twitter, Reddit and forums). The dominant emotions were disgust, anger and joy. Pair with BeerBoard bar-pour data (Axios) and YouGov tracking.
course_use: Illustrates the social-listening module of a brand audit and its limits (volume ≠ representativeness). Free

title: Lessons from the Bud Light boycott, one year later (Kellogg Insight)
author_source: Kellogg School of Management / Kellogg Insight, 2024
note: Academic one-year retrospective on the Bud Light crisis, a ready reflection piece to close a brand crisis audit (what happened to loyalty, what brand managers should learn).
course_use: Reading after the Darden case/YouGov data. Free

title: Can Volkswagen salvage its damaged brand? (Gallup Business Journal)
author_source: Gallup Business Journal, 2015
note: Practitioner analysis of VW's apology and goodwill package after Dieselgate, arguing that emotional customer engagement data shows much more is needed. A short evidence-based commentary on a German brand crisis.
course_use: Reading with the Ivey/INSEAD VW cases; students design a brand-trust tracking plan. Free

title: Julius Meinl: neuer Markenauftritt 'I do it MEINL way' (2024)
author_source: Leadersnet.at, Aug 2024; agency Obscura
note: Viennese heritage coffee brand (founded 1862) repositions toward a 'Coffee Love Brand' to rejuvenate its target group. A live Austrian rejuvenation example where students can audit heritage cues vs. the new identity.
course_use: Topic for a student brand audit (Austrian heritage brand). Free

title: Almdudler: erfrischend neuer Markenauftritt
author_source: about-drinks.com; agency Dirnberger de Felice Grüber
note: First new claim and brand presence in almost 30 years, explicitly meant to 'strengthen what was there from the start' rather than reinvent the brand. A clear 'evolution, not revolution' example that reflects the Tropicana lesson, set in an Austrian brand. Plus a distribution change in Germany (own distribution from 2027).
course_use: Topic for a student brand audit/discussion of continuity of brand elements. Free

title: How adidas got its mojo back (Walter Scott, 2025)
author_source: Walter Scott & Partners, investment research article, June 2025
note: Analysis of the German brand's turnaround under Bjørn Gulden. Diagnosis: product/marketing sidelined by strategists, wholesale neglected. Fix: product at the centre, retailers back on side, heritage lines (Samba, Gazelle, Spezial) scaled up. A good example of heritage brand assets as the basis for revitalization.
course_use: Mini-case for revitalization via heritage; students verify with adidas annual reports and brand rankings. Free

title: Alexis Nasard on transforming Swarovski into a modern pop-luxury brand (IMD)
author_source: I by IMD interview, Dec 2024
note: First-hand CEO account of repositioning a Tyrolean family brand: three product categories with distinct price and style tiers, a tiered collection from entry level to bespoke rather than across-the-board price increases, and 2023 revenue of EUR 1.83 bn. Primary-source input for a Swarovski brand audit.
course_use: Pair with the free 'World of Swarovski' case. Free

title: Österreichs Studierende wollen für Red Bull und Google arbeiten (Universum Austria)
author_source: Leadersnet.at, Universum 'Most Attractive Employers Austria' (10,125 students surveyed), 2018
note: Employer-brand audit data for Austria: business students rank Red Bull 1st, then Google and BMW; engineering/IT students rank Google, Siemens, Microsoft. Shows how employer-brand rankings feed an employer brand audit. Note: older edition; current results are on universumglobal.com.
course_use: Employer-brand audit module: compare a brand's consumer vs. employer brand standing. Free
